summary:
Developed using the Atoms.dev platform, Space Mission Architect is a Unity WebGL-based 2D space mission design and management simulation featuring a dark/cyberpunk NASA control panel interface. The project offers a 6-tier campaign ranging from Low Earth Orbit to deep-space Voyager probes.

Players design modular spacecraft by managing trade-offs between Budget ($), Mass (kg), Net Power (W), and Science Points. Powered by the Atoms.dev infrastructure, the system includes part buying/selling, part damage/durability mechanics affected by space crises, pre-launch success rate percentage calculations, and a budget rollover system where leftover funds from previous missions carry over.

This tool transforms complex aerospace and engineering constraints into an accessible experience, teaching how technical limitations impact mission success.
details:
Developed using the Atoms.dev platform and designed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge, Space Mission Architect is a 2D space mission design and management simulation playable via browser on a Unity WebGL infrastructure, featuring a modern dark/cyberpunk NASA control panel interface.

The project's detailed architecture, gameplay mechanics, and technical features are organized under the following headings:

1. Project Concept and Visual Interface (UI/UX)

To offer players the experience of a real NASA flight engineer, the project operates with a professional 3-panel mission control design:

  • Left Panel (Part Catalog): Houses components across various categories such as solar panels, RTG nuclear generators, deep-space antennas, cameras, spectrometers, and support modules.
  • Center Panel (Assembly & Slot System): The workspace where the player drags and drops parts onto a modular rocket schematic or manages component slots.
  • Right Panel (Live Telemetry & NASA Codex): Updates Budget ($), Mass (kg), Net Power (W), and Mission Science (Points) counters in real time. Additionally, the "NASA Codex" info box explains the historical and technical applications of selected parts in real space missions.

2. Four-Variable Engineering Model (Trade-Offs)

Players must balance 4 core variables to gather the maximum amount of scientific data under limited resources:

  • Budget ($): The financial limit allocated for the mission.
  • Mass (kg): The maximum payload capacity the rocket can carry.
  • Net Power (W): The balance between generated power (solar panels/RTGs) and consumed power (cameras, antennas, sensors) — must satisfy $\text{Net} \ge 0$.
  • Mission Science (Points): The game's primary score and success criterion.

3. Extended Level System and Carry-Over System

The game offers a 6-tier campaign stretching from Low Earth Orbit to the edge of deep space:

  1. LEO Earth Observation Satellite (Base Budget: $400k | Mass: 300kg | Solar Efficiency: 100%)
  2. Geostationary Communications Satellite (Base Budget: $550k | Mass: 400kg | Solar Efficiency: 90%)
  3. Artemis Lunar Surface Rover (Base Budget: $700k | Mass: 520kg | Solar Efficiency: 67%)
  4. Mars Surface Rover (Base Budget: $1.1M | Mass: 800kg | Solar Efficiency: 34%)
  5. Jupiter / Europa Orbiter Probe (Base Budget: $1.6M | Mass: 1100kg | Solar Efficiency: 8% - RTG Mandatory)
  6. Deep Space Voyager Probe (Base Budget: $2.2M | Mass: 1500kg | Solar Efficiency: 0% - Deep Space)

Savings Carry-Over: Players do not lose unspent money upon completing a mission; this amount is added to the next mission's budget as a "Bonus Budget." Even if a player fails in higher levels, the accumulated bonus funds are retained, encouraging cost-efficient engineering.

4. Advanced Gameplay Mechanics

  • Part Buying and Selling (Buy/Sell): Any component placed in the assembly panel can be removed from its slot at will; its cost is immediately refunded to the budget, while mass and power values are restored in telemetry.
  • Part Health and Damage System (Durability): Solar storms, micrometeoroid impacts, or radiation waves occurring during the operational phase reduce component durability. Parts dropping below 50% health lose efficiency, while those reaching 0% are completely disabled. Thermal armor and shielding mitigate this damage.
  • Pre-Launch Success Rate Calculator (%): Prior to launch, power margin, mass limit, protective shielding, and communications capacity are factored together to calculate and display the project's estimated success percentage.

5. Significance of the Project

Space Mission Architect transforms abstract aerospace and engineering principles into an engaging, interactive puzzle experience. Running seamlessly on the web via the Atoms.dev infrastructure, this simulation intuitively teaches students and space enthusiasts the vital role of technical constraints, budget management, and risk analysis in space exploration.
